sources.author: Swyx Wang
sources.headline: AI Engineer & Founder @ Latent Space | Building the AI Engineer community
sources.post_summary: Claude's new extended thinking mode is showing 40%+ improvement on multi-step agentic tasks in our internal benchmarks. The trick isn't just more tokens — it's that the model now backtracks and self-corrects mid-chain. This fundamentally changes how you architect tool-calling loops. Thread on what this means for agent framework design.

sources.author: Hamel Husain
sources.headline: AI Consultant | Former GitHub, Airbnb, Netflix | Making ML actually work in prod
sources.post_summary: Hot take: 90% of 'AI agent' demos you see on LinkedIn are single-turn LLM calls with a for loop around them. Real agents need memory, interruption handling, and graceful degradation. Here's a checklist I use to evaluate whether a system is actually agentic or just expensive autocomplete with extra steps.

sources.author: Gergely Orosz
sources.headline: Author of The Pragmatic Engineer | Engineering leadership & software craft
sources.post_summary: Six months ago I asked 200 senior engineers if they used AI coding tools daily. 34% said yes. I asked again last week: 81% said yes. The holdouts aren't skeptics anymore — they're mostly folks blocked by enterprise security reviews. The bottleneck has shifted from adoption to procurement and compliance.

sources.author: Cassie Kozyrkov
sources.headline: Chief Decision Scientist | AI Strategy | Ex-Google | Making AI safe and useful
sources.post_summary: The infrastructure bottleneck for AI agents isn't compute — it's observability. You can't debug a multi-agent system you can't trace. We're still running 2019-era logging practices on 2026-era autonomous pipelines. OpenTelemetry support for LLM spans is the unsexy thing every AI infra team needs to prioritize this quarter.

sources.author: Alicia Marsh
sources.headline: Head of Revenue Operations @ Momentum | GTM Systems | Ex-Salesforce
sources.post_summary: Shared a breakdown of how her team cut their outbound sequence build time from 3 days to 4 hours by moving sequence ownership from SDRs to a centralized GTM engineer. Argued that 'sales personalization' at scale is an ops problem, not a rep problem, and that most RevOps teams are still solving it backwards. Post included a before/after diagram of their Clay → Instantly → Salesforce stack.

sources.author: Derek Fontaine
sources.headline: GTM Engineer | Building AI-native outbound systems | Newsletter: The Signal Stack
sources.post_summary: Posted a contrarian take arguing that 'AI SDRs' are a distraction and that the real leverage is in AI-enriched signal routing — getting the right prospect to the right rep at the right moment, not replacing the rep entirely. Backed it with a screenshot of a signal stack he built using job change alerts, LinkedIn intent, and G2 review triggers piped into a Slack channel. Over 200 comments debating whether outbound is dead.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: VP of Marketing @ Corvo | Pipeline-Obsessed | B2B Content & Demand Gen
sources.post_summary: Shared a content strategy teardown showing how her team generates 60% of their demo requests through a 'teach-to-convert' content loop: long-form how-to posts that rank on LinkedIn search, repurposed into newsletter sequences, with a soft CTA to a free audit tool. Called out the difference between content that builds brand and content that builds pipeline, and why most B2B teams confuse the two.

sources.author: Jason Tully
sources.headline: Sales Ops Lead @ Archetype | CRM Nerd | Ops That Closes Deals
sources.post_summary: Went viral after posting a raw breakdown of how a poorly maintained Salesforce instance cost their team an estimated $280K in missed pipeline last year — through duplicate leads, broken routing rules, and reps working stale accounts. Framed it as 'your CRM is either an asset or a liability, there is no middle ground,' and offered a free 10-point audit checklist in the comments that got thousands of downloads.
